The confound the triage flagged is not a side issue but the dominant one: on 2026-08-11 KMB cut FY2026 guidance to an adjusted-EPS DECLINE at a low-single-digit constant-currency rate on a China diaper disruption worth ~100bp of full-year growth (3-4pp off International Personal Care organic, 10-12pp off its operating profit), and management explicitly framed integration progress as greater confidence in the EXISTING $1.9B target, not more synergies — so no new number was put on the table. Deal close therefore resolves an overhang the tape does not show exists (KVUE trades at a 2.4% spread to the $19.25 implied deal value, i.e. the market already prices a near-certain close), while leaving the actual cause of the drawdown, China and category growth, entirely unresolved. Per the provenance rule this is scored as the equity, not the event: cap 4, WATCH, and it converts to ACTIVE only on evidence of China stabilization or a raised/accelerated synergy number.

verified.catalyst: Closing of the $215.4M related-party drop-down from Kimbell's sponsor (announced 17 Jul 2026, ~2,568 net royalty acres / 2,347 boe/d) on or around 21 Aug 2026, with management having committed to reset 2026 guidance upon that close.
verified.dated_milestone: Drop-down close on or around 2026-08-21; guidance reset published at/after close (KRP affirmed 2026 guidance on 2026-08-06 and said it "expects to update guidance upon the closing of the Drop Down"). Full P&L recognition lands in Q3 2026 results (early Nov 2026).
verified.bloom_gates: G1 PASS (named counterparty: affiliated sellers / Kimbell sponsor group, board + Conflicts and Compensation Committee approved 2026-07-16). G2 PASS (concrete committed consideration: $74.9M cash + 9.5M newly issued OpCo units valued $140.5M, effective date 2026-06-01, close ~2026-08-21). G3 FAIL — no specific currently-unpriced figure: accretion is stated only as "immediately accretive to distributable cash flow per unit" with no quantum, and the guidance raise is mechanically computable from the 2026-07-17 release (2,347 boe/d on 25,830 boe/d base, ~9%), so it is knowable and therefore priced.
verified.edge: L — run-up from pre-catalyst base is +0.7% (7/16 close $14.80 -> $14.91 on 8/18), so the event is genuinely unharvested; but the prize itself is tiny. Re-derived remaining capture to favorable resolution is only ~+2-4% ($15.20-15.50), because the acquisition economics are roughly neutral, not a dislocation. Everything beyond that is an oil/gas price bet.
verified.primary_source: Kimbell 8-K/press release "Kimbell Royalty Partners, LP Announces $215.4 Million Drop Down Acquisition" (2026-07-17, SEC CIK 0001657788 accession 0001104659-26-084429); Q2 2026 results release (2026-08-06/07) affirming 2026 guidance and stating guidance will be updated upon closing of the Drop Down; FMP quote/EOD chart pulled 2026-08-18 ($14.91, 52wk 11.31-15.80).
verified.analysis: Numerator provenance re-derived from the capital structure rather than inherited: KRP has NO preferred ahead of the common (the old Series A is gone), $478.7M revolver debt at ~1.4x TTM EBITDA on a $660M borrowing base, and ~98.6M units ($1.47B cap / $14.91) — so the waterfall is clean and any accretion accrues to the common. But the arithmetic does not support a meaningful prize: the 9.5M OpCo units are ~9.6% dilution, while the acquired 2,347 boe/d scaled off Q2's $103.0M oil/gas/NGL revenue on 25,830 boe/d implies ~$37M revenue and ~$24-28M of cash flow after royalty-margin and revolver interest on the $74.9M cash slug — roughly an 11-13% cash yield paid for with equity issued at a ~16.8% DCF yield ($2.51/unit annualized off the $0.47 Q2 distribution at 75% payout). That makes the deal flat-to-marginally-dilutive on DCF/unit on my numbers, against management's unquantified "immediately accretive" claim; per the FIP rule I therefore score the EQUITY, not the event, and cap at 4. It is a real, dated, forward, non-macro corporate event (close ~Aug 21, guidance reset committed), which keeps it on WATCH — but it is accretion mechanics in a conflicted sponsor drop-down, the units sit 5.6% under the $15.80 52wk high and 6.3% over the 200dma, and realized return from here is dominated by commodity prices rather than by the transaction.
